subject: AWS PO request — approval lanes & term-flex plan for DataWave
messages:
From: Julie Harper <julie@datawave.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement - DataWave <procurement@datawave.io>; AWS Marketplace PM <mpm@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2024 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Private Offer — 3yr term + buyer approval path

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — DataWave is excited about integrating Redwood for inference at scale. Procurement asked me to follow up with the specifics for an AWS private offer so they can route approvals. Key asks from their side:

- Pricing target: prefer a 20% list discount for a 36-month commitment (goal: predictable unit cost)
- Term: 36 months, with the option to renew at fixed uplift in year 3
- Buyer approval path: initial procurement signoff -> legal review -> VP budget approval (if ARR impact > $250k)

I've attached a draft PO and procurement's preliminary approval matrix. Can Redwood confirm whether the 36-month term is supported for a private offer and what internal approvals or pricing floors you need? Also please indicate any required SOC/infra addenda or required SLAs to include.

Thanks — Julie

Attachments: DataWave-AWS-PO-draft-v2.pdf, approval-matrix.xlsx

--
Julie Harper
Head of Partnerships, DataWave Analytics
julie@datawave.io

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Julie Harper <julie@datawave.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2024 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Private Offer — 3yr term + buyer approval path

Julie —

Appreciate the clear asks and the attachments. Short answers up front: we can do a private offer with a 36-month term, but pricing floor and approval routing depend on committed monthly spend and whether you need Dedicated capacity or Hosted API quotas pinned.

Proposed next steps so we don't block procurement:

1) Internal approval lanes: I'll route pricing for review (Vanessa) and high-level legal/term review (Karthik). If the buyer's ARR impact threshold (~$250k) is correct, Jonas can prepare the seller-side approval matrix we use for private offers that cross that threshold.
2) Pricing options: propose two lanes for DataWave to present to their buyer committee:
   - Lane A (Hosted, non-dedicated): 18% list off, no SLA uplift, suitable if they accept shared capacity
   - Lane B (Dedicated pool + reserved capacity): 25% list off, includes 99.9% uptime SLA and dedicated support window
3) Term constructs: we can support 36 months; for renewals we typically add a fixed CPI-like uplift cap (max 5% year-over-year). We can make renewal optional in the PO language.
4) Compliance addenda: SOC2 attestation and network architecture diagram can be attached. If they need on-prem/private deployment, that changes pricing lanes.

Can Vanessa, Jonas, and Karthik weigh in on the pricing floor and whether procurement requires additional evidence for buyer approvals? If acceptable, I'll prepare a short mutual action plan for Julie's procurement team.

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2024 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private Offer — 3yr term + buyer approval path

Folks —

Quick pricing guidance based on similar deals in the SMB analytics vertical:

- For a public hosted PO with sustained monthly usage below $100k, our standard floor is 15% off list. For sustained commits > $100k/mo we can go to 22–28% depending on commitment and whether they prepay.
- Dedicated capacity adds material operational cost — aim for a delta of ~6–9% above Hosted lane when building the offer. Bundled support and SLA are typical negotiation levers.
- Long terms (36 months) should include migration/exit language: 90-day notice for scaling down, prorated refunds for unused committed credits (if prepay). Legal likes a cap on termination liability for marketplace POs.

Buyer approval thresholds (internal seller side):
- Pricing < $250k ARR equivalent: channel manager signoff + marketplace ops (no exec approval)
- Pricing between $250k-$1M: require Sales Lead + Finance approval
- Pricing > $1M: require VP/GM approval + Sales Ops and Legal signoff

I'll attach a quick draft approval-lane spreadsheet and annotate the recommended lane for DataWave based on the numbers Julie sent.

Vanessa

Attachment: approval-matrix.xlsx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Julie Harper <julie@datawave.io>; Procurement - DataWave <procurement@datawave.io>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2024 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: Private Offer — approval lanes & term notes

Hannah / Julie / team — forwarding an updated approval matrix and proposed language for the private offer. Summary:

- Recommended lane: Hosted PO + 30% list discount if DataWave commits to $120k/mo sustained usage for 36 months (equivalent to ~ $5.18M TCV). This hits our "> $1M" threshold so VP approval will be required.
- If DataWave prefers Dedicated pool, propose 36-month with 25% list discount and an additional managed-service add-on at a fixed monthly fee; this keeps TCV slightly higher but simplifies SLA handling.
- Renewal clause: automatic renewal at previous term pricing unless either party gives 60-day notice; opt-out triggers re-pricing.
- Compliance: attaching SOC2 summary and the standard marketplace SLA addendum.

Attachments: approval-matrix.xlsx, DataWave-AWS-PO-draft-v2.pdf

Jonas
